items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: I had been listening to the records... when I heard he was coming to the Town Casino of course I showed up... I was very disappointed at first, but then when I heard them I said, well yeah, this might be okay

ctx.x: Did you get the impression, once you started playing the bass, I’m going to guess that your listening habits started centering more on that part of the music and you start to learn patterns and hearing them before you even went to play them.

Yes. Yeah absolutely. I had — when I was in Germany, when I first started in Germany I had a bunch of records. We had what they call a BX or base exchange that had a lot of records. It had a nice record selection. And so I wound up with a couple of hundred albums in my room in the barracks you know. And another early experience that affected my whole life was New Year’s Eve 1963. I was going into my — well actually I was in the middle of my senior year. Because I graduated in June of ’64. So yeah it was my junior…
He couldn’t get anybody good, huh?
